BPF scheduler operation callbacks, enqueue and dispatch paths, and slice replenishment timing
Runqueue integration, task selection, preemption and migration decisions
Cgroup scheduler attach, move, weight and bandwidth enforcement mechanics
Enabled housekeeping mask management, partition updates and affinity application
CPU hotplug teardown ordering and idle-task lifecycle beyond the empty hook
NUMA balancing policy and data structures
Final address-space free path, user-reference teardown and next-owner selection

findings.text: Per-task extensible-scheduler entity keeps dispatch membership as a queue pointer plus list and tree nodes for FIFO and vtime ordering, with a sequence counter and queue-owned flags alongside runqueue-owned flags and an operation sequence. It also stores weight and a count of consecutive reenqueues.

The same entity tracks CPU placement with several CPU identifiers for stickiness, holding, selection and current runnability, where negative runnability means not runnable. It links into a runqueue runnable list with a timestamp and optionally records rescue-queue time and cgroup move source under build options.

Identity and scheduler-owned runtime state comprise a persistent non-zero task identifier with a hash node, a remaining runtime budget, a vtime key for priority queues, and an atomic out-of-band slice request. Two kernel-task pointers and a global tasks list node are also present.

Control and diagnostic area holds a flag refusing later entry into the extensible policy and, only while a capability-reject reenqueue condition holds, the missing capability bits and target identifier. An RCU scheduler pointer exists only with cgroups support.

Task-group extension object is empty unless group scheduling is enabled, in which case it holds a scheduler pointer, flag and weight words, bandwidth period quota and burst intervals, and an idle marker.
CPU idle classification enumerates four ordered values covering not idle, idle, newly idle, and a count sentinel marking the number of kinds.
Housekeeping kinds order boot domain, dynamic domain, managed IRQ, kernel noise, then a max sentinel. Kthread aliases dynamic domain. Tick, timer, RCU, misc and workqueue all alias kernel noise.

Job control stop and trap bit positions are 16 through 24 consecutively for dequeued, pending, consume, trap stop, trap notify, trapping, listening, trap freeze and ptrace frozen, plus 26 for stopped and 27 for traced.

Job control masks use low 16 bits for the stop signal number. Single-bit masks shift one by each bit position above, trap mask combines the two trap bits, and pending mask combines stop pending with the trap mask.

Load average fixed point uses 11 fractional bits, unity as one shifted by that width, sampling every five seconds plus one tick, and decay factors 1884, 2014 and 2037 for one, five and fifteen minutes.
Integer and fractional load helpers shift down by the fixed-point width and scale the fractional remainder by one hundred before shifting.

Membarrier process states occupy bits 0 through 7 as ready and armed pairs for private expedited, global expedited, private sync-core and private rseq. Command flags use bit 0 for sync-core and bit 1 for rseq.

Polling helpers make the polling flag visible before sampling need-reschedule, with ordering paired against the reschedule path. Clearing also folds a pending reschedule so the caller observes it without an IPI.

Three polling builds exist: arch atomic bit operations, generic bit operations, and a fallback where set and clear are empty and the combined test only samples need-reschedule while clear still orders against reschedule and folds.

With isolation disabled, housekeeping reports the local CPU, the possible mask, disabled state, affinity as no effect, every CPU present, and update returning success with empty init. Isolation is defined as absence from the domain set.
When isolation support is compiled in, the per-CPU housekeeping query consults the dynamic test only if an override static branch is active; otherwise it reports present unconditionally.
Load calculation blends old load weighted by decay with active count weighted by the complement, rounds up by nearly one unit when active reaches or exceeds old load, then scales back by unity.

Scheduler pointer updates occur at fork or while holding both the task pi lock and the runqueue lock. Queue-owned flags are protected by the dispatch-queue lock while runqueue-owned flags and operation sequence are protected by the runqueue lock.
Vfork detection holds RCU across dereference of the real parent and comparison of address spaces, because parent linkage can change under clone variants that separate parent from creator.

Address-space lifetime separates structural and user references: grab and user-get increment respective counters, drop decrements and frees at zero with barrier semantics, and a scheduler variant may defer the final free through RCU.

Lazy-TLB reference handling is conditional on build support: when enabled it forwards to the normal grab and drop paths including the deferred scheduler drop, and when disabled the drop paths still provide a full barrier.
Default memory placement helpers return task size as mapping end, echo the supplied base, do nothing for layout selection and owner update unless overridden elsewhere.

Effective allocation context masks request flags from current task state: no-IO clears both IO and filesystem use and wins over no-filesystem, no-filesystem clears filesystem use, and pin clears movability.
Allocation-context save sets requested task flags and returns which bits changed so restore can clear exactly those bits; dedicated wrappers exist for no-IO, no-filesystem, no-reclaim and pin modes.
Active memory-cgroup selection returns the previous scope: interrupt context uses a per-CPU slot while task context uses a current-task field; a disabled build always returns null.

Polling lifecycle moves between polling and non-polling with an immediate need-reschedule sample on each transition. Leaving polling restores IPI delivery for future reschedule requests and folds any already pending request.

Job control state groups stop intent, trap requests and terminal conditions: pending combines stop-pending with stop and notify traps, trap mask combines the two traps, and stopped versus traced record which stop path was taken.

Changing the vtime key while queued can corrupt priority ordering. The runtime budget is cleared on a forced preemption and must not be used for executed-time accounting. Capability-reject details are valid only while the reject condition holds.

Refusing extensible policy is only meaningful when set during scheduler load initialization: setting it then reverts an already-extensible task and counts a rejection, while setting it on later per-task initialization fails the scheduler.

Address-space release relies on decrement barrier semantics for the membarrier path, and lazy-TLB drops must barrier even without refcounting. Vfork detection can miss when the creator used parent or thread sharing with an unkillable reaper.

Group scheduler pointer is tracked separately from the cgroup pointer because hierarchy shape and lifetime can diverge: removed groups can outlive cgroup removal and stale pointers are not revisited, and controller mounting can differ.
Task identifier is assigned once at fork, never zero, never reused, and survives exec, allowing scheduler logic to name tasks without retaining kernel pointers.
Out-of-band slice state packs pending status, issuer identity and requested amount into one atomic word, applied later under the runqueue lock when the issuer lacks it at request time.

Memory-allocation wait marks the caller uninterruptible, adjusts flags by current context, then sleeps briefly when blocking is allowed and retry permitted, otherwise sleeps longer after releasing locks.
Allocation-context check brackets reclaim acquire and release, bypasses sleep checking when the caller holds the no-reclaim flag, and otherwise warns if blocking allocations could sleep.
Vfork test reports true only when the task has a completion object and its address space matches its real parent address space under RCU.

Disabled or fallback scheduler hooks do nothing or report negative: extensible death and info, soft and hard lockup probes, RCU stall probe, idle exit, hotplug wait hooks as null, tickless enter remote start stop and wake, and membarrier switch exec and update.
Sync-core-before-usermode is skipped unless arch support exists, the examined space is the current one, and the private sync-core expedited state is set; only then is the arch synchronization issued.
